title: Mathematics AA HL - Set A - Paper 3

questions.stem: The circle $C$ has equation $x^2+y^2=25$. The point $P=(3,4)$ lies on its upper semicircle, written $y=f(x)$. Coordinates are measured in millimetres. In parts(b)to(e), consider the differential equation $\mathrm dy/\mathrm dx=-x/y$, with $y=4$ when $x=3$, taking the positive branch near this point.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.prompt: Use implicit differentiation to show that $\mathrm dy/\mathrm dx=-x/y$ on $C$ where $y\ne0$.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the tangent to $C$ at $P$.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.prompt: State, with a reason, whether the differential equation is separable.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.prompt: State, with a reason, whether it is homogeneous in the sense $y\prime=F(y/x)$.

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.prompt: State, with a reason, whether it is a first-order linear equation in $y$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Solve the initial-value differential equation to obtain an implicit equation relating $x$ and $y$.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.prompt: Use Euler's method with step size $0.1$, starting at $(3,4)$, to estimate $y$ when $x=4$.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of $y$ at $x=4$ and explain why the Euler estimate is an overestimate.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.prompt: Show that $\dfrac{\mathrm d^2y}{\mathrm dx^2}=-\dfrac{x^2+y^2}{y^3}$.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the Maclaurin approximation to $f(x)$ through the term in $x^2$.

parts.label: e(iii)
parts.prompt: Use this approximation to estimate $f(4)$.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: A particle moves on $C$. At the instant it passes through $P$, its $x$-coordinate is increasing at $8$ mm s$^{-1}$. Find the rate of change of its $y$-coordinate at that instant.

questions.answerSummary: Tangent $y-4=-3(x-3)/4$; implicit solutioncircle; Euler3.0324aboveexact3; quadratic3.4; verticalrate-6mm/s.

steps.text: Yes: putting $v=y/x$ gives $y\prime=-1/v$ wherever the substitution is defined.
No: the right-hand side depends on $1/y$; it cannot be written $y\prime+P(x)y=Q(x)$ as an equation in $y$.
Thus $x^2+y^2=25$, with the positive branch selected near the initial point.
The upper semicircle is concave down over the interval, so successive forward tangent steps lie above its exact solution.
Differentiate with respect to time: $2x\,\mathrm dx/\mathrm dt+2y\,\mathrm dy/\mathrm dt=0$.

questions.stem: For an integer $n\ge2$, consider the equation $z^n=1$. Write $\operatorname{cis}\theta=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ and define $z_k=\operatorname{cis}(2\pi k/n)$ for integer $k$. Any $n$ consecutive indices give all distinct roots. Let $S_n$ and $P_n$ be respectively the sum and product of these $n$ distinct roots. You may use $S_n=0$ for $n\ge2$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Verify that every $z_k$ satisfies $z^n=1$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State a formula for $P_n$ in terms of $n$.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.prompt: For $n=3$, write $z_{-1},z_0,z_1$ in Cartesian form.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.prompt: Use these roots to calculate $P_3$.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.prompt: For $n=4$, write $z_{-1},z_0,z_1,z_2$ in Cartesian form.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.prompt: Use these roots to calculate $P_4$.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Show that $(z-z_k)(z-z_{-k})=z^2-2z\cos(2\pi k/n)+1$.

parts.label: f(i)
parts.prompt: For $n=6$, list all six roots in cis form using the indices $-2,-1,0,1,2,3$.

parts.label: f(ii)
parts.prompt: Write $z_3$ in Cartesian form for $n=6$.

parts.label: f(iii)
parts.prompt: Factorize $z^6-1$ as a product of real linear and real quadratic factors.

parts.label: g(i)
parts.prompt: For $n=5$, list all five roots in cis form using indices $-2,-1,0,1,2$.

parts.label: g(ii)
parts.prompt: Factorize $z^5-1$ into one real linear and two real quadratic factors, leaving cosine coefficients exact.

parts.label: h
parts.prompt: Write down the analogous real factorization of $z^7-1$.

parts.label: i
parts.prompt: Using $S_5=0$, prove that $\cos(2\pi/5)+\cos(4\pi/5)=-1/2$.

parts.label: j(i)
parts.prompt: Write down $\cos(2\pi/7)+\cos(4\pi/7)+\cos(6\pi/7)$.

parts.label: j(ii)
parts.prompt: For $m\in\mathbb Z^+$, write down the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^m\cos\left(\frac{2k\pi}{2m+1}\right)$.

questions.answerSummary: $P_n=(-1)^{n+1}$; conjugate pairing gives the real factorizations; odd-root cosine sums equal $-1/2$.

steps.text: The paired roots are $\cos\phi\pm i\sin\phi$, where $\phi=2\pi k/n$.
Take the real part of the sum of all five roots.
Division by2 gives the required result.
